messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Turning a messy CSV into something useful
parts:
I have a bunch of regions with food data, but instead of being organized as a single table, it's organized in multiple tables. Not all regions have all food items (data sample attached).

I need it organized with foods as rows and region_category as columns, like so:

1. Codigo producto Ozama o Metropolitana_Casos Ozama o Metropolitana_% Ozama o Metropolitana_Acumulado % Cibao Norte_Casos Cibao Norte% Cibao Norte_Acumulado %
Pan de agua 1766433 2.38 2.38 114499 0.29 0.29
Pan sobado 528508 0.71 3.09 815476 2.06 2.35
Pan de leche 3270 0 3.09 2729 0.01 2.36
Pan de maíz 907 0 3.1 376 0 2.36
Pan de mantequilla 7294 0.01 3.11 2427 0.01 2.37
Pan baguette 6175 0.01 3.11 4016 0.01 2.38

(3 separate data.frames with casos, %, and acumulado % is also fine)

Any thoughts on how to approach this? I don't mind doing some manual editing of the CSV, but I will probably need to do this process more than once so getting it mostly done via code is important.


--
Thanks,
Erica


Erica Rettig
PhD Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Turning a messy CSV into something useful
parts:
This is a bit of an ugly solution, but it seems to work:

# import and fix Erica's data:

datasample <- read.csv("~/Desktop/brdug/drug-datasample.csv", header=FALSE, comment.char="#")

# I think we first need to split this into one data frame per region:

header = which(datasample[,1]=="1. Codigo producto")
region1 = datasample[header[1]:(header[2]-4),]
region2 = datasample[header[2]:(header[3]-4),]
region3 = datasample[header[3]:nrow(datasample),]

# Now change the names of the variables
names(region1) = c("Condigo", "R1_Casos", "R1_%", "R1_Acumulado")
names(region2) = c("Condigo", "R2_Casos", "R2_%", "R2_Acumulado")
names(region3) = c("Condigo", "R3_Casos", "R3_%", "R3_Acumulado")

# get rid of the first lines
region1 = region1[-1,]
region2 = region3[-1,]
region3 = region3[-1,]

# Now merge the data sets together

fulldata = merge(region1, region2, by = "Condigo", all.x = T, all.y = T)
fulldata = merge(fulldata, region3, by = "Condigo", all.x = T, all.y = T)

# However, for a lot of analyses, you might want your data in this format instead:
region1$region = rep(1, nrow(region1))
region2$region = rep(2, nrow(region2))
region3$region = rep(3, nrow(region3))

names(region1) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")
names(region2) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")
names(region3) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")

fulldata2 = rbind(region1, region2, region3)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Turning a messy CSV into something useful
parts:
I took a bit of a different approach, but it seems to work.

## Data
pp <- "~/Downloads/drug-datasample.csv"

## Read in data as lines to find where to separate
doc <- readLines(pp)

## Look for headings
idx <- grep("AREA", doc)

## Length of each table, accounting for spaces before and after "AREA" line
nr <- diff(c(idx, length(doc) + 2)) - 2

## Read in each table separately
ans <- lapply(seq_along(idx), function(i)
    read.csv(pp, skip = idx[i] + 1, nrows = nr[i] - 2))

## Get area info
area_info <- strsplit(doc[idx], ",")

## Add area info to data.frames
ans <- lapply(seq_along(ans), function(i) {
    x <- ans[[i]]
    x$area <- area_info[[i]][1]
    x$area_nm <- area_info[[i]][2]
    return(x)
    })

## Combine
do.call(rbind, ans)

Matt

>         I need it organized with foods as rows and region_category as columns, like so:
>
>         1. Codigo producto    Ozama o Metropolitana_Casos     Ozama o Metropolitana_%         Ozama o Metropolitana_Acumulado %       Cibao Norte_Casos       Cibao Norte%    Cibao Norte_Acumulado %
>         Pan de agua   1766433         2.38    2.38    114499  0.29    0.29
>         Pan sobado    528508  0.71    3.09    815476  2.06    2.35
>         Pan de leche  3270    0       3.09    2729    0.01    2.36

>         Pan baguette  6175    0.01    3.11    4016    0.01    2.38
>
>
>         (3 separate data.frames with casos, %, and acumulado % is also fine)
>
>         Any thoughts on how to approach this? I don't mind doing some manual editing of the CSV, but I will probably need to do this process more than once so getting it mostly done via code is important.

parts:
Jaime - that's it, thanks! I knew it was something simple.

The other suggested solutions didn't work, just for reference:

Rbind doesn't work - you end up with many repetitions of the same food.

        X1..Codigo.producto   Casos   X. Acumulado..       area               area_nm
1               Pan de agua 1766433 2.38        2.38 AREA # 110 Ozama o Metropolitana
...
16              Pan de agua  114499 0.29        0.29 AREA # 201           Cibao Norte


> test <-  do.call(merge, append(dta2, list(by = "food", all = TRUE)))
Error in fix.by(by.x, x) :
  'by' must specify one or more columns as numbers, names or logical
On Wed, Aug 10, 2016 at 12:52 PM, Duncan Temple Lang <dtemp...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:

Hi Erica

I've not spent more than a few seconds looking at this so ignore if it is not the case, but probably
your list(dta2, by = "food", all = TRUE) should be

 append(dta2, list(by = "food", all = TRUE))

The latter is a list with two more elements than dta2
and the former is a list with three elements

On 8/10/16 11:35 AM, Erica Rettig wrote:
> With a bit of code stolen from Rosie, I've got this nearly solved. The last step is that I need to call do.call for merge, but I keep getting an error:
>
>> do.call(merge, list(dta2, by="food", all=T))
> Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE,  :
>   arguments imply differing number of rows: 15, 13, 19
>
> I don't think that all=T is getting passed properly. Can anybody spot what's going on? Full code attached.
>
> On Tue, Aug 9, 2016 at 8:48 PM, Rosemary Hartman <roseh...@gmail.com <mailto:roseh...@gmail.com>> wrote:
>
>     This is a bit of an ugly solution, but it seems to work:
>
>     # import and fix Erica's data:
>
>     datasample <- read.csv("~/Desktop/brdug/drug-datasample.csv", header=FALSE, comment.char="#")
>
>     # I think we first need to split this into one data frame per region:
>
>     header = which(datasample[,1]=="1. Codigo producto")
>     region1 = datasample[header[1]:(header[2]-4),]
>     region2 = datasample[header[2]:(header[3]-4),]
>     region3 = datasample[header[3]:nrow(datasample),]
>
>     # Now change the names of the variables
>     names(region1) = c("Condigo", "R1_Casos", "R1_%", "R1_Acumulado")
>     names(region2) = c("Condigo", "R2_Casos", "R2_%", "R2_Acumulado")
>     names(region3) = c("Condigo", "R3_Casos", "R3_%", "R3_Acumulado")
>
>     # get rid of the first lines
>     region1 = region1[-1,]
>     region2 = region3[-1,]
>     region3 = region3[-1,]
>
>     # Now merge the data sets together
>
>     fulldata = merge(region1, region2, by = "Condigo", all.x = T, all.y = T)
>     fulldata = merge(fulldata, region3, by = "Condigo", all.x = T, all.y = T)
>
>     # However, for a lot of analyses, you might want your data in this format instead:
>     region1$region = rep(1, nrow(region1))
>     region2$region = rep(2, nrow(region2))
>     region3$region = rep(3, nrow(region3))
>
>     names(region1) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")
>     names(region2) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")
>     names(region3) = c("Condigo", "Casos", "Percent", "Acumulado", "region")
>
>     fulldata2 = rbind(region1, region2, region3)
>
>
>     On Tue, Aug 9, 2016 at 3:14 PM, Erica Rettig <erica....@gmail.com <mailto:erica....@gmail.com>> wrote:
